name: Peru
summary_text: Peru demands real caution with a nationally-legislated bathroom ban and documented police violence against trans people, but no criminalisation of trans identity and an unprecedented 17-year conviction for police torture of a trans woman. Congress approved (February-April 2025) a bathroom ban prohibiting trans people from using public bathrooms matching their gender — a nationally-legislated axis-C restriction comparable to US state bans or the UK EHRC code. A consumer-protection body dismissed a trans woman's discrimination complaint against a gym that enforced the policy. Between 2020 and 2023, 54 TLGBI people were assassinated (trans women most affected). In the Azul Rojas Marín case, three police officers were sentenced to 17 years for torture and sexual abuse of a trans woman (December 2025) — an unprecedented conviction for Peru and the Inter-American Court of Human Rights. A presidential decree briefly classified trans identity as a "mental disorder" (May 2024), but was walked back after massive protests. For a visitor: no border friction, but the bathroom ban creates daily legal exposure when using public facilities.

sources.title: Congreso aprueba norma que atenta contra el derecho de las personas trans a usar baños públicos - Infobae
sources.claim_summary: Infobae (Feb 2025, in Spanish): Peru's Congress Women and Family Commission unanimously approved a bill barring people from using public sanitary facilities designated for the sex opposite to their birth sex (bills 6506 and 8457 by Montoya and Muñante); activist Gianna Camacho called it discriminatory; also bans 'ambiguous' signage in bathrooms.

sources.title: Discriminación legalizada: sobre la prohibición del Congreso a personas trans para acceder a baños públicos - IDEHPUCP
sources.claim_summary: IDEHPUCP (PUCP human-rights institute) analysis (in Spanish): 'Discriminación legalizada' - commentary on the Peruvian Congress's prohibition of trans people accessing public bathrooms, analysing the measure as legalised discrimination.

sources.title: Perú: aumentaron los crímenes de odio y las mujeres trans son las más afectadas - Agencia Presentes
sources.claim_summary: Presentes (July 2024, in Spanish): hate crimes increased in Peru and trans women are the most affected - 54 murders of TLGBI people and 170 rights violations 2020-2023 per the Cayetano Heredia University Observatory; documents the extortion-killing of trans sex worker Rubí Torres Silvano by the 'Los Gallegos' criminal gang, with victims' bodies filmed as extortion threats.

sources.title: 17 años de prisión para 3 policías en Perú por violar y torturar a una persona trans, en una condena inédita para el país y la Corte Interamericana de Derechos Humanos - BBC News M
sources.claim_summary: BBC Mundo (Dec 2025): 17 years' prison for three Peruvian police officers for raping and torturing trans woman Azul Rojas Marín - the first conviction in Peru for a case of discrimination-based sexual torture, and the first Inter-American Court case recognising discrimination-motivated torture in the region (2008 case, Casa Grande).

sources.title: Agresores de Azul Rojas reciben condena casi 20 años después: PJ dicta 17 años de prisión contra los policías Dino Ponce, Luis Quispe y Juan León - Infobae
sources.claim_summary: Infobae (Dec 2025, in Spanish): the Azul Rojas aggressors receive their sentence almost 20 years later - 17 years' effective imprisonment; the first time Peruvian justice convicted state agents for prejudice-motivated sexual torture of an LGBTI person, fulfilling Inter-American Court measures (Peru publicly acknowledged responsibility and apologised in 2022).

sources.title: Peru: New Law Threatens Free Speech, Trans Rights | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (May 2025): 'Peru: New Law Threatens Free Speech, Trans Rights' — a crime-prevention law's vague provisions chill expression and endanger trans people's rights.

sources.title: Peru Walks Back Anti-Trans Guidance in Health System | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jun 2024): 'Peru Walks Back Anti-Trans Guidance in Health System' — health ministry reverses guidance classifying trans identities as 'mental health problems' requiring conversion-style assessment.

sources.title: Peru | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): one of the few South American countries not recognising same-sex couples; trans people can rectify name/gender markers only via an expensive, complicated court process taking years; a 2017 law bans SOGI discrimination but violence persists and hate crimes go unpunished; in 2024 the Health Ministry unexpectedly issued a decree classifying trans identity as a mental-health condition.

sources.title: A Week of Setbacks: Gender, LGBTQ+ and Reproductive Rights Under Attack in Peru | Peru Support Group
sources.claim_summary: Peru Support Group (April 2025): 'A week of setbacks' - Congress approved bills 6505/2023-CR and 8457/2023-CR banning people from using public bathrooms counter to their birth sex and banning inclusive signage; criticised by the Ombudsman's Office; part of a broader rollback of gender, LGBTQ+ and reproductive rights.

sources.title: Peruvian Congress Votes to Remove LGBT from Hate Crime Legislation | The Perchy Bird
sources.claim_summary: The Perchy Bird (May 2017): Peru's Congress voted 66-29 to remove LGBT terms from hate-crime legislation, repealing the section of President Kuczynski's January 2017 decree that had extended hate-crime protections to sexual orientation and gender identity after a million-signature petition; Peru returned to being one of three South American countries with no LGBT anti-discrimination laws (with Paraguay and Guyana).
